P1.evidence: The application was read and used later to open a thread — 'because in the application form, I saw that ... you're acquiring oil and gas mineral rights' — and the prospect confirmed he had written notes in it, so the read-back check is met. The frame was three-part: 'I just want to understand what's going on. What have you tried? What are you trying to get to. And if there's an alignment, we can definitely talk about it.' No 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was not asked for; the prospect said 'Yep' and immediately launched into his history, which also took the place of the open question.

P2.evidence: The most thorough baseline in the batch. Age, weight and height all confirmed directly. Diet was taken meal by meal across two days rather than in the abstract. Sleep was asked and then followed sensibly into breathing — 'do you snore or something like that?' Energy was asked twice including on a scale. Injuries were the spine of the first ten minutes with dates, mechanisms, imaging and treatment. Work, travel and sitting all covered. P2c is partial because there was no open health-conditions question: the cholesterol history and the holistic cardiologist emerged through the diet thread, and the allergies through the sleep thread. P2f is partial — what his current on-and-off training is producing was never directly asked.

P3.evidence: 'But why do you want to get shredded?' produced the real answer immediately, and the rep sharpened it — 'And you encounter it every single day when you tie your shoes.' The longevity driver was then developed properly: 'being fit for the later stages of life, how does it actually show up for you? What does it mean for you, specifically?' led to muscle mass as a predictor of longevity and to his parents at 80. The reflect-back was the best line of the call — 'reclaiming the athlete that is already there inside you, we need to surface him up' — which the prospect took and improved, 'Retune it.' P3f was never asked: a fiancée, two young stepdaughters, grown children and a son in Singapore were all discussed and nobody was ever tied to the outcome.

P4.evidence: Prior attempts, what happened and why it stopped were all covered, including the useful probe 'when you were playing at D1, did you have to go to the gym?' followed by 'So why did you stop?' — 'I hated it.' The prospect named the gap unaided and precisely: 'The problem is guidance on getting from point A to point B' and 'I know what to do, but I don't know what order to get in.' P4f is partial because the rep substituted a reframe for the question — 'you're not lacking discipline or motivation. You just don't like boring gym stuff' — which worked, the prospect accepting and adding 'And guidance.'

P5.evidence: Not run in any form. No two-year question, no settle-for challenge, no why-not, no line in the sand. Every piece of consequence material in the call was volunteered by the prospect — his parents at 80, the man at the UPS store, 'I don't want to wait till I'm 75 and can't do anything' — and by the rule that the script credits asking rather than luck, this is a miss on all four. It closed anyway, which is the point worth recording: this prospect arrived with his own urgency, so the phase that carries most deals was never tested here.

P6.evidence: P6b ran early and before anything was presented — 'apart from not having the structure, is there anything that would keep you, that would stop you from actually moving forward with this?' — 'No.' P6a ran after the pillars: 'if you had the right nutrition, the right training, and the accountability, all designed around your life, around your schedule, do you agree like you would actually get to the goal' — 'Oh, yeah. Yep.' Commitment was then re-taken twice more, before the price ('are you committed to showing up and doing the work?') and before the payment link ('just to be sure, you're 100% on this').

P11.evidence: The only complete Phase 11 in the batch and it was run in order without a gap. Payment collected live through a Stripe link in the Zoom chat and confirmed on both sides. Onboarding call with Trevor booked from offered slots, and the prospect made to open the confirmation email and accept the invitation on the call. The agreement was confirmed as received, read and signed live — 'Could you just go through it and sign it so you get all the rest of the materials?' — with the prospect confirming a copy of the signed document. TrueCoach access, the Skool community invitation and the onboarding form were each named in advance and then each confirmed as received. The only blemish is a term the rep had not covered and could not explain cleanly when the prospect read it out of the contract.

objection_plays.detail: No money objection at any point. The prospect anchored above the price himself — 'How much does it cost? 20 grand?' — and asked only about mechanics. The coached line was used correctly for the how-do-I-pay question: 'Most guys just put it on credit card or debit card up front.' Worth flagging for coaching in the other direction: the rep then volunteered the split unprompted, 'What I would advise, if you want to split it, split it in half', to a prospect who had shown no price resistance and had not asked to spread it. That is $3,000 of collection deferred for no concession gained.
No delay or deliberation trigger. The prospect asked for next steps himself: 'What's the next steps? Email? Just give me all the data or what?'
No spouse trigger. A fiancée was discussed warmly and never as a decision input.

No timing objection. The prospect corrected the rep's own deadline framing upward rather than downward — told 'let's get you in the best possible shape before summer', he replied 'I don't care about before summer. That's like in a week.'

No fear or doubt trigger. The nearest thing was risk management rather than doubt — 'if I get an injury halfway through, no fault of Trevor's, then I'm stuck' — offered as a reason to split the payment.

Injury-risk concern with no scripted play. The prospect raised the possibility of being injured mid-programme and it drove his payment structure decision. The rep answered with a policy commitment made on the spot — 'No, if you get an injury, we pause' — that appears nowhere in the playbook and is not evidenced in the signed agreement. There is no scripted position on pausing, deferring or refunding for injury, which for an offer built on loaded ballistic training and sold to people with injury histories is a conspicuous gap.

notes: Very strong through baseline, goals, root cause and commitment, and a textbook Phase 11 that should be the reference recording for onboarding — payment, booking, signature and welcome materials all completed and verified before hanging up. Two corrections despite the outcome. Phase 5 was never run: the prospect supplied his own consequence and the rep took it, so nothing here demonstrates the rep can build urgency where it does not already exist. And the split payment was offered to a buyer who had anchored at $20,000 and never asked for one.
